title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-13
ranking_basis: Daily GitHub Trending star gains for 12 entries; 3 GitHub Search recent-creation additions appended with daily gains unavailable.
ranking_explanation: The twelve repositories visible on GitHub Trending?since=daily are sorted by the page’s “stars today” values. sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time: 2026-11-13 17:26 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-13 through 2026-11-13. Ranking basis: daily Trending star gains, with recent-creation Search additions appended separately.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Coding-agent infrastructure led today’s page: Google Chrome’s web-guidance source gained 1,875 stars, followed by Sure and OpenAI Codex Security. The mix also includes a personal-finance app, encrypted networking, monitoring, and new graphics/runtime experiments.

sections.title: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src
sections.description: Source and tooling for Modern Web Guidance, a CLI-delivered set of expert-curated web-platform skills for coding agents.
sections.why_notable: The day’s largest star gain, with an unusually concrete agent workflow: search, retrieve, and scan for legacy web patterns using compact, evaluated guidance.
sections.unique_caveat: The trending repository is the source repo; its README points to a separate distribution repository and developer.chrome.com documentation.

sections.title: we-promise/sure
sections.description: A self-hostable personal-finance and wealth-management application with browser, desktop, mobile, API, and agent access.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest daily gain, showing strong interest outside the AI tooling cluster in a full-featured, community-maintained personal-finance app.
sections.unique_caveat: README identifies it as a community fork of the now-abandoned Maybe Finance project.

sections.title: openai/codex-security
sections.description: OpenAI’s Codex Security CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating, and fixing security vulnerabilities.
sections.why_notable: A major daily surge at the intersection of coding agents and application security; the README documents CLI scans, policy drafts, exports, CI workflows, and findings storage.
sections.unique_caveat: Some documented scanning and provider workflows require API credentials; scan results still need human review.

sections.title: tailscale/tailcat
sections.description: A netcat-like tool and Go library that sends traffic over Tailscale’s encrypted data plane without its control plane.
sections.why_notable: A strong infrastructure signal: it packages WireGuard-encrypted peer connections into a lightweight CLI/library, with out-of-band exchange of connection metadata.
sections.unique_caveat: Direct peer-to-peer connectivity depends on NAT traversal; DERP relay is the fallback, and the browser demo is relay-only today.

sections.title: ZhuLinsen/daily_stock_analysis
sections.description: An LLM-powered multi-market stock-analysis system combining market data, news, decision dashboards, and scheduled notifications.
sections.why_notable: A sizable daily gain for a domain-specific agent application; its README details multi-market data sources, analysis workflows, web UI, and scheduled delivery.
sections.unique_caveat: README warns that free upstream data sources can be rate-limited or unstable; output quality depends on configured data and model providers.

sections.title: Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo
sections.description: A Windows video and capture enhancement tool described as combining AI super-resolution, DLSS 5 enhancement, and frame generation.
sections.why_notable: A distinct desktop media/rendering counterpoint to the agent-heavy list, with 245 stars gained today.
sections.unique_caveat: The GitHub description makes ambitious DLSS 5 and PS5/GTA6 framing claims; Trending/API metadata does not independently verify compatibility or performance.

sections.title: alibaba/open-code-review
sections.description: A hybrid code-review tool combining deterministic pipelines and LLM agents, with multi-language rules and line-level comments.
sections.why_notable: Its hybrid design makes it a notable code-quality pattern: deterministic checks handle repeatable rules while an LLM agent contributes review context.

sections.title: ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
sections.description: Chrome DevTools exposed to coding agents through the Model Context Protocol.
sections.why_notable: Adds a browser-inspection and debugging surface to the agent toolchain, complementing guidance and security projects in today’s list.

sections.title: backnotprop/plannotator
sections.description: A workspace for annotating, reviewing, sharing, and feeding plan/code feedback back to coding agents.
sections.why_notable: Represents human-in-the-loop agent work: feedback is attached to plans and code rather than left in a disconnected chat.

sections.title: block/buzz
sections.why_notable: A high-visibility Rust project that broadens the daily list beyond individual developer utilities into collaborative communication.
sections.unique_caveat: The short repository description is not enough to establish detailed architecture or deployment characteristics.

sections.title: louislam/uptime-kuma
sections.why_notable: An established infrastructure project still appearing in today’s Trending results, a useful counterpoint to newer agent-focused repos.

sections.title: tradermonty/claude-trading-skills
sections.description: Claude Code skills for equity analysis, charting, economic calendars, screening, and trading-strategy development.
sections.why_notable: A smaller but clear example of specialized task skills extending a coding-agent interface into a domain workflow.

sections.title: apex-compute/ANR
sections.description: Apex Neural Rendering: frame-generation tooling, with super-resolution and ray-reconstruction components also announced.
sections.why_notable: A freshly created graphics repository found in GitHub Search, adding a new performance/rendering signal beyond the Trending page.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says frame generation is in beta, other components are forthcoming, and source code is not yet available; GitHub Search provides no daily star delta.
sections.ranking_source: GitHub Search recent-creation supplement; daily gain unavailable

sections.title: deepseek-ai/chat-demo
sections.description: A static TypeScript chat client that calls the configured DeepSeek API directly from the browser, without an application backend.
sections.why_notable: Created on November 12 and pushed on November 13; it is a fresh, first-party lightweight AI application, not yet represented in the daily Trending view.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says the API key and settings are stored in browser localStorage and conversations in IndexedDB; GitHub Search provides no daily star delta.
sections.ranking_source: GitHub Search recent-creation supplement; daily gain unavailable

sections.title: makepad/relax
sections.description: An experimental Rust JIT/runtime that runs Cargo packages from source, compiles functions on demand, and patches edits into a running process.
sections.why_notable: Created November 11 and actively pushed today; it proposes a different Rust development loop focused on live-edit iteration rather than production builds.
sections.unique_caveat: README labels the project experimental and says testing has focused mainly on Makepad’s own loop; it also reports slower optimized code than rustc release builds. GitHub Search provides no daily star delta.
sections.ranking_source: GitHub Search recent-creation supplement; daily gain unavailable

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The clearest shared trend is making agents more usable and accountable through curated context, security checks, browser tooling, and human review. At the same time, Sure’s momentum and the continued presence of self-hosted infrastructure show that practical applications remain part of the story. Newly created Search discoveries are listed separately because GitHub does not provide their daily star gains.
